kept.excerpt: Atlético de Madrid and Manchester City have reached an agreement for the transfer of Julián Alvarez, who has signed for the club until 2030. The club said the Argentine forward signed a contract for the next six seasons.
kept.relevance: The official signing establishes Atlético as his contracted club and shows that a departure in summer 2026 would require ending or transferring a long-term contract.

kept.excerpt: After Argentina’s World Cup victory over Austria, Alvarez publicly requested a departure from Atlético: “I spoke to Atlético people, and I think the best for everyone involved is for me to leave.” Sports Illustrated reported that Barcelona’s approximately €100 million offer had been rejected.
kept.relevance: His public request to leave and a rejected Barcelona bid establish concrete transfer pressure despite Atlético’s resistance.

kept.excerpt: The RFEF disciplinary committee opened extraordinary disciplinary proceedings against Barcelona over Julián Alvarez. The report said Barcelona had submitted an offer of €100 million payable in instalments, while Atlético had publicly and privately maintained that the player was not for sale and referred to his €500 million release clause.
kept.relevance: The reported proceedings and Atlético’s stated release-clause position identify obstacles to completing his preferred transfer.

kept.excerpt: Marcos Llorente, Álex Baena, Julián Alvarez and Juan Musso returned to work on Monday, August 10, and underwent medical examinations. The club said the internationals would follow individual exercise plans supervised by its fitness staff before joining the group.
kept.relevance: This official update confirms Alvarez had returned to Atlético’s preseason programme rather than remaining absent to force a transfer.

kept.excerpt: Coach Diego Simeone again insisted on Tuesday that Julian Alvarez would not leave Atlético Madrid that year, saying he wanted to “build a team around” the Argentina striker. While on World Cup duty, Alvarez had said he believed a transfer was best for everyone without confirming his preferred destination.
kept.relevance: Simeone’s statement immediately before the cutoff indicates that Atlético’s sporting plans continued to depend on retaining Alvarez.

kept.excerpt: Barcelona had established an updated timetable for pursuing Alvarez, according to this report citing Mundo Deportivo. The reported deadline was the next two or three days, after which the sporting management would activate an alternative if the transfer remained unresolved; Atlético continued to regard Alvarez as not for sale.
kept.publisher: Get Spanish Football News via Yahoo Sports
kept.relevance: The reported short deadline supplies a near-term catalyst for whether Barcelona would continue pursuing a transfer before September 1.

kept.excerpt: Atlético president Enrique Cerezo reiterated that the club had never intended to sell Alvarez and said he was confident the player would win back the supporters within two matches. The report said Barcelona’s summer pursuit had included a single €100 million offer.
kept.relevance: The club president’s cutoff-day comments provide recent attributable evidence that Atlético still intended to retain Alvarez.

kept.excerpt: Alvarez was not called up by Simeone for Atlético’s opening league fixture. La Nación reported that the player remained dissatisfied with the lack of a resolution to his desired Barcelona transfer and that Atlético had rejected a €100 million offer.
kept.relevance: This cutoff-day account documents continuing dissatisfaction and an unresolved transfer request alongside the club’s public retention stance.
